changes.before: (*dioston*)
changes.after: (*diosmon*)

changes.before: Augustine's twenty-two books On the City of God
changes.after: Augustine's twenty books On the City of God

changes.before: since he [Hilary] dealt
changes.after: since he [Lucifer] dealt

changes.before: The term is δίοσμον (*diosmon*); the transliteration in the text should read *diosmon*.
changes.after: The term is δίοσμον (*diosmon*).

changes.before: so I have translated 'twenty' — correction: the Latin reads twenty, and the translation should reflect it; see text.
changes.after: but the Latin is translated as it stands.

changes.before: The bracketed '[Hilary]' should read '[Lucifer]' or be treated as uncertain; the subject is only implied.
changes.after: The subject is only implied.

changes.before: "As Sappho against the Mytilenaeans" is obscure; the reference may be confused or corrupt.
changes.after: The wording is compressed; the sense supplied in brackets is how the name Sappho is inflected among the Mytilenaeans.

changes.before: translated loosely as 'he records'
changes.after: translated as 'the people of Ios'

changes.before: 'later in his works' may mean 'inferior in his achievements'.
changes.after: 'Inferior in his works' renders a word that can also mean 'later'.

changes.before: "Alta" is probably a misreading of Afranius, author of *togatae*.
changes.after: "Alta" is taken as Atta, an author of *togatae*.

changes.before: The phrase 'paid no attention to anyone' renders μηδενὶ προσέσχε τὸν νοῦν literally; perhaps 'to none of them'.
"The [war] for the souls" (τὸν δὲ περὶ τῶν ψυχῶν) is elliptical;
changes.after: "The [war] in which lives were at stake" (τὸν δὲ περὶ τῶν ψυχῶν, literally "the one for the souls") is elliptical;

changes.before: the rendering of the title is uncertain and "Aeginetic" should be deleted.
changes.after: the rendering of the title is uncertain.

changes.before: "Bone-generating" for ὀστεογενῆ is uncertain; the word could also mean "bone-derived".
changes.after: "Bone-born" for ὀστεογενῆ is uncertain; the word could also mean "bone-generating".

changes.before: 'Later' (ὕστερον/ὑστέραν) may also carry the sense 'inferior'.
changes.after: 'Inferior' renders ὑστέραν, which can also mean 'later'.

changes.before: μειοῖ ('lessens') makes poor sense; read as αὔξει ('increases') or similar, which the context requires.
changes.after: μειοῖ ('lessens') is translated as printed. The translator thought it made poor sense and that αὔξει ('increases') or similar might be meant.

changes.before: I have rendered 'auction' in error-free transliteration as 'ausion' would be: read 'ausion'.
changes.after: it is transliterated here as 'ausion'.

changes.before: Mistake in my rendering of Hecataeus' form: read 'Abotieus' (Greek Ἀβοτιεύς) for 'Aboticus'.
changes.after: Hecataeus' form is Abotieus (Greek Ἀβοτιεύς).

changes.before: "εἰς ἀνδρὸς ἰέναι" taken as "come to manhood"; it could also be read as "enter a man's house", i.e. marry.
changes.after: "εἰς ἀνδρὸς ἰέναι", literally "enter a man's house", is taken as "marry a husband".

changes.before: Translated loosely.
the translation follows the likely reading kai\ kai/ria ("missiles") as given, but the sense is uncertain.
changes.after: the translation takes kai/ria as "with deadly aim", but the sense is uncertain.

changes.before: Augustine's own gloss implies "while the fear lasted", and the translation leaves this ambiguous.
changes.after: Augustine's own gloss implies "while the fear lasted", but the translation follows the usual sense.

changes.before: read as Stromateis (Στρωματεῖς).
changes.after: read as Exegetika.

changes.before: "Homer forming [it] from martys"
changes.after: "Homer forming [the word] from martyros"

changes.before: The gloss ὡμοίωϲαι is printed as given; it may stand for ὡμοίωϲαϲ, 'you likened'.
The comma in 'δράσουσι κατὰ, αὑτῶν' is misplaced; read as 'κατʼ αὑτῶν' (against themselves).
changes.after: 'κατὰ' in 'δράσουσι κατὰ, αὑτῶν' is read as κακά ('evils').

changes.before: The phrase οὔθ’ ὅλως καλὸν νομίζοντα is awkward: literally '[you] who do not at all think it fine to sell'. As it stands this seems to contradict the context, so a negative may be misplaced or the text corrupt. I have translated what the context requires: the addressee does not consider selling philosophy wrong.
changes.after: The phrase οὔθ’ ὅλως καλὸν νομίζοντα is taken to refer to the writer, Socrates, who does not think it at all right to sell.
